_**User (2026-08-28 06:12:35Z)**_

我現在要製作一個skill是我的Python best practice 特別是for agentic coding的時代
不過我現在會把我所有想法列出來 你需要再幫我統整一下 順便看有沒有漏掉的

1. 一定用uv來做package management 且最好是足夠新的版本 (src/package-name) => README 要有getting started user知道怎麽uv sync等等
2. 製作CLI的話使用Tyro (並且注意shell的auto completion) -> 合理切分subcommmand modules => 方便下游user可以直接uv tool install (不一定要直接deploy PyPI 可以先讓user從git link來install)
3. notebooks 使用marimo notebook 且notebook可以有script mode (一樣用Tyro) 這樣多種interface (WebUI/CLI 都能有相同體驗) 非package的notebook應該要放 notebooks/
  - notebooks 可以做爲package的使用範例
  - package 可自帶anywidget 特別是一些特殊visualize
4. logging使用loguru
5. 最好都有CLI 並且同時在 AGENTS.md (symlink to CLAUDE.md) 確保每次更新package都能同步更新skill (甚至可以學herdr 把skill直接做進)
6. 推薦如果scaffold項目自帶我們的skills
  - agent-history-hygiene
  - project-knowledge-harness
  - mkdocs-site-bootstrap => 所有public項目都有良好的github page docs說明 (給人類看 ; 給agent看有llms.txt)
7. 此skill也可以用作舊的Python項目的refactor依據指南
8. TDD driven development始得loop engineering可驗收
9. 項目以外的helper放到 scripts之中
10. 製作Justfile把常用操作放進去 或是考慮用 [tool.taskipy.tasks] ？
11. 我們的package要維護一個自己的agent skill 讓agent知道如何調用
12. 我們應該會要有一個scaffold CLI for此purpose (可以是一個Tyro uv script讓AI調用 並保證可控)
13. 如果有API server設計考慮FastAPI + Pydantic等 (需有Swagger/OpenAPI說明頁)
14. 如果agent skill不夠涵蓋的部分可以考慮製作MCP
15. agentic是一個選項 不過也可以初始最簡 後面有需要再慢慢加上去
16. 也考慮有Rust backend + PyO3的開發指南
17. 考慮項目類型可能帶額外推薦skill 比如ML項目等等 可能會考慮帶上 experimentknowledge-harness 等等
18. linting formatting 考慮 ruff, black等 (setup LSP?)


Optional setup

```
❯ cat .envrc
# https://github.com/direnv/direnv/issues/1264
# .envrc
# export VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv
# layout python3
# [[ -d ".venv" ]] || . .venv/bin/activate

# .envrc
# 自動啟動 .venv
# since direnv cannot modify PS1, won't got prompt like `(.venv) $`
# unless you configure PS1 in your shell rc file
export VIRTUAL_ENV="$PWD/.venv"
export PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"

# 如果有 .env 就載入
dotenv_if_exists
```


核心要點

1. clear
2. portable
3. plug and play
4. easy to use
...

由繁至簡都可以用
從0 setup還是舊項目refactor也可以用
普通情況就是Python dev guide 但可以避免許多過時的開發

1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43	auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44	symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45	
46	```bash
47	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48	```
49	
50	Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51	
52	| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55	| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56	| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57	
58	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60	
61	> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62	> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63	> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
64	> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
65	> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
66	> out without further prompting.
67	
68	After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
69	`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
70	follow-up actions deterministically.
71	
72	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73	
74	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75	that matter most:
76	
77	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79	  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80	  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81	  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89	  escape hatches.
90	
91	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93	happens"), not just that it exists.
94	
95	### 4. Design any scripts
96	
97	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100	requirements:
101	
102	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108	
109	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111	have to set up an environment first.
112	
113	### 5. Lint
114	
115	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116	
117	```bash
118	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119	```
120	
121	It checks three things:
122	
123	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124	   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125	   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
127	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
128	   script).
129	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
130	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
131	
132	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
133	
134	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
135	
136	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
137	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
138	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
139	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
140	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
141	
142	## Available scripts
143	
144	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
145	  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
146	  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
147	  table in step 2.
148	  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
149	    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
150	    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
151	  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
152	    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
153	    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
154	    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
155	    symlinks).
156	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
157	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
158	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
159	- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
160	  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
161	  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
162	  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
163	  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
164	  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
165	  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
166	  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
167	    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.
168	
169	## Bundled assets
170	
171	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
172	
173	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
174	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
175	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
176	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
177	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
178	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
179	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
180	
181	## Reference files
182	
183	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
184	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
185	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
186	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
187	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
188	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
189	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
190	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
191	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
192	
193	## Gotchas
194	
195	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
196	  symlink with a real file.
197	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
198	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
199	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
200	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
201	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
202	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
203	- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
204	  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
205	  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
206	  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
207	- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
208	  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
209	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
210	  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
211	  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
212	  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
213	  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
214	  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
215	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
216	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
217	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
218	  investing in authoring.
219	- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
220	  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
221	  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
222	  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
223	  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
224	  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
225	  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
226	- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
227	  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
228	  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
229	  if you ever hand-create one, see
230	  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).
231	
232	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
233	
234	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
235	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
236	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
237	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
238	quantitative validation.
239

```text
1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
221	
222	```markdown
223	# [Analysis Title]
224	
225	## Executive summary
226	[One paragraph]
227	
228	## Key findings
229	- Finding 1 with supporting data
230	- Finding 2 with supporting data
231	
232	## Recommendations
233	1. Specific actionable recommendation
234	2. Specific actionable recommendation
235	```
236	````
237	
238	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
239	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
244	
245	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
246	
247	```markdown
248	## Form processing workflow
249	
250	Progress:
251	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
252	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
253	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
254	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
255	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
256	```
257	
258	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
259	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Validation loops
264	
265	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
266	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
267	
268	```markdown
269	## Editing workflow
270	
271	1. Make your edits.
272	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
273	3. If validation fails:
274	   - Read the error message.
275	   - Fix the issues.
276	   - Run validation again.
277	4. Only proceed when validation passes.
278	```
279	
280	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
281	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Plan-validate-execute
286	
287	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
288	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
289	
290	```markdown
291	## PDF form filling
292	
293	1. Extract form fields:
294	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
295	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
296	3. Validate:
297	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
298	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
299	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
300	5. Fill the form:
301	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
302	```
303	
304	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
305	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
306	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
307	
308	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
309	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## Bundling reusable scripts
314	
315	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
316	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
317	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
318	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
319	
320	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
321	
322	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
323	agent can call them reliably.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Quick checklist before commit
328	
329	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
330	
331	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
332	      not just a one-line summary
333	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
334	      <=1024 chars required
335	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
336	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
337	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
338	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
339	      listed at the bottom
340	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
341	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
342	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
343	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
344	      `--dry-run` support
345	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
346	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
347
```

```text
1	# This-repo conventions
2	
3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills
4	authored elsewhere may follow different rules; this file is the source of
5	truth for **this** repo.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	skills/
11	├── local/             # skills authored in this repo (committed in full)
12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md
14	│       ├── references/
15	│       ├── scripts/
16	│       └── assets/
17	└── vendor/            # skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
18	    └── <skill-name>/
19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **New skills authored here go in `skills/local/`.** Always.
23	- **Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`** — it gets overwritten by
24	  the next `make sync`. Upstream changes go through `vendor.yaml` + `make sync`.
25	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
26	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
27	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
28	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
29	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The
30	  `new-skill.sh` scaffolder creates these symlinks automatically in **LOCAL
31	  mode**; never add new *canonical* skill content directly under them here.
32	
33	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
34	
35	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
36	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
37	precedence (when no flag given):
38	
39	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
40	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
41	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
42	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
43	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
44	   discovery symlinks for you.
45	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
46	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
47	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
48	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
49	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
50	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
51	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
52	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
53	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
54	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.
55	
56	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
57	already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
58	"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
59	behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
60	
61	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
62	the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
63	(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
64	the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
65	for the historical bug this convention prevents.
66	
67	## Skill discovery
68	
69	The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:
70	
71	1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
72	2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
73	   useful.
74	
75	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
76	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
77	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
78	
79	## Scripts naming and mirroring
80	
81	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
82	root. The pattern:
83	
84	| Canonical location | Mirror |
85	|---|---|
86	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
87	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
88	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
89	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |
90	
91	Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
92	via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
93	targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.
94	
95	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
96	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
97	automated check for this — be careful.
98	
99	## Documentation
100	
101	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
102	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
103	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
104	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
105	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
106	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
107	
108	When you add a new local skill, also add:
109	
110	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
111	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
112	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
113	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
114	
115	## Project memory
116	
117	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
118	
119	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
120	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
121	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
122	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
123	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
124	
125	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
126	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
127	
128	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
129	
130	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
131	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
132	
133	## Bash compatibility
134	
135	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
136	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
137	escape hatches.
138	
139	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
140	
141	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
142	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
143	repo**. Notable specifics:
144	
145	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
146	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
147	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
148	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
149	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
150	  parsing-heavy helpers.
151	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
152	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
153	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
154

```text
1	# Script design for agent skills
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/using-scripts>. Read this
4	before adding anything to `scripts/` in a skill.
5	
6	The headline difference from "regular" CLI design: **the caller is an LLM that
7	reads your stderr to decide what to do next.** Optimize for that.
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [One-off commands vs bundled scripts](#one-off-commands-vs-bundled-scripts)
12	2. [Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`](#pin-versions)
13	3. [Self-contained scripts (PEP 723 etc.)](#self-contained-scripts)
14	4. [Agentic CLI design rules](#agentic-cli-design-rules)
15	5. [Error message style](#error-message-style)
16	6. [Structured output](#structured-output)
17	7. [Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes](#idempotency-dry-run-exit-codes)
18	8. [Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)](#bash-32-compatibility-macos)
19	9. [Quick script checklist](#quick-script-checklist)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## One-off commands vs bundled scripts
24	
25	If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, **don't
26	bundle a script** — reference the tool directly:
27	
28	```bash
29	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
30	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
31	```
32	
33	Bundle a script when:
34	
35	- The invocation grows past ~3 flags or needs computed arguments.
36	- You need to compose multiple tools.
37	- The logic must be tested independently.
38	- You want to give the agent a stable interface even if the underlying tool
39	  changes.
40	
41	State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md` ("Requires Node 18+", "Requires
42	`uv`"). Don't assume the agent's environment.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Pin versions
47	
48	Unpinned `uvx`, `npx`, `pipx` invocations behave inconsistently as upstreams
49	release new versions. Always pin:
50	
51	```bash
52	# Good
53	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
54	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
55	pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .
56	
57	# Bad — silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change
58	uvx ruff check .
59	npx eslint --fix .
60	```
61	
62	`@latest` is fine **if** the skill explicitly says "tracks upstream latest" and
63	the user understands that.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Self-contained scripts
68	
69	When a script needs dependencies, prefer **inline declarations** over a
70	sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with
71	one command and no setup.
72	
73	### Python — PEP 723
74	
75	```python
76	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
77	# /// script
78	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
79	# dependencies = [
80	#   "beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5",
81	# ]
82	# ///
83	"""Extract <p class="info"> from an HTML file."""
84	import sys
85	from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
86	
87	with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
88	    html = f.read()
89	print(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").select_one("p.info").get_text())
90	```
91	
92	Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html`. `uv` creates an isolated
93	environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically.
94	
95	For full reproducibility, `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py` produces
96	`scripts/extract.py.lock`.
97	
98	### Deno
99	
100	```typescript
101	#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run
102	import * as cheerio from "npm:cheerio@1.0.0";
103	// ...
104	```
105	
106	### Bun
107	
108	```typescript
109	#!/usr/bin/env bun
110	import * as cheerio from "cheerio@1.0.0";
111	// ...
112	```
113	
114	If a `node_modules/` exists anywhere up the tree, Bun's auto-install is
115	disabled. Mention this in the skill if relevant.
116	
117	### Ruby
118	
119	```ruby
120	require 'bundler/inline'
121	gemfile do
122	  source 'https://rubygems.org'
123	  gem 'nokogiri', '~> 1.16'
124	end
125	# ...
126	```
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Agentic CLI design rules
131	
132	### No interactive prompts, ever
133	
134	Agents run in non-interactive shells. A script that calls `read`, `input()`,
135	or any TTY prompt **hangs indefinitely**. There is no recovery.
136	
137	```
138	# Bad
139	$ python scripts/deploy.py
140	Target environment: _
141	
142	# Good
143	$ python scripts/deploy.py
144	Error: --env is required. Options: development, staging, production.
145	Usage: python scripts/deploy.py --env staging --tag v1.2.3
146	```
147	
148	Accept all input via flags, env vars, or stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).
149	
150	### `--help` is the primary documentation
151	
152	The agent reads `--help` to learn the script. Make it concise but complete:
153	
154	```
155	Usage: scripts/process.py [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE
156	
157	Process input data and produce a summary report.
158	
159	Options:
160	  --format FORMAT    Output format: json, csv, table (default: json)
161	  --output FILE      Write output to FILE instead of stdout
162	  --verbose          Print progress to stderr
163	  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it
164	
165	Examples:
166	  scripts/process.py data.csv
167	  scripts/process.py --format csv --output report.csv data.csv
168	
169	Exit codes:
170	  0  success
171	  1  invalid arguments
172	  2  input file not found
173	  3  processing failed
174	```
175	
176	The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Error message style
181	
182	When an agent gets an error, the message **directly shapes its next attempt**.
183	Opaque errors waste turns.
184	
185	```
186	# Bad
187	Error: invalid input
188	
189	# Good
190	Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table.
191	       Received: "xml"
192	```
193	
194	Pattern: **what was wrong + what was expected + what to try.**
195	
196	For "field not found" style errors, include the available alternatives in the
197	message — this lets the agent self-correct without re-querying the system:
198	
199	```
200	Error: Field 'signature_date' not found.
201	       Available fields: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed.
202	```
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Structured output
207	
208	Prefer JSON / CSV / TSV / NDJSON over whitespace-aligned columns. Structured
209	output is parseable by both the agent and standard tools (`jq`, `cut`, `awk`).
210	
211	```
212	# Bad
213	NAME          STATUS    CREATED
214	my-service    running   2025-01-15
215	
216	# Good
217	{"name": "my-service", "status": "running", "created": "2025-01-15"}
218	```
219	
220	**Separate data from diagnostics.** Send structured data to stdout; send
221	progress, warnings, debug logs to stderr. The agent can then `jq` stdout
222	cleanly while still seeing diagnostics if it wants.
223	
224	Bash convention:
225	
226	```bash
227	log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }   # diagnostics → stderr
228	log "Loading config from $CONFIG"
229	printf '{"status":"ok"}\n'           # data → stdout
230	```
231	
232	---
233	
234	## Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes
235	
236	### Idempotency
237	
238	Agents retry. "Create if not exists" beats "create and fail on duplicate".
239	"Apply migration if not applied" beats "apply migration".
240	
241	### `--dry-run`
242	
243	For destructive or stateful operations, `--dry-run` lets the agent preview
244	and the user confirm. Implement it as a real preview (show what would change),
245	not a no-op:
246	
247	```
248	$ scripts/deploy.sh --dry-run --env staging --tag v1.2.3
249	[dry-run] Would deploy v1.2.3 to staging.
250	[dry-run] Would update 3 services: api, worker, scheduler.
251	[dry-run] Would run post-deploy hook: scripts/healthcheck.sh.
252	```
253	
254	### Exit codes
255	
256	Use distinct codes for distinct failure types. Document them in `--help`.
257	This lets the agent branch retry/recover behavior:
258	
259	| Code | Meaning |
260	|---|---|
261	| 0 | success |
262	| 1 | invalid arguments / usage |
263	| 2 | required input missing or not found |
264	| 3 | external system failure (network, auth, dependency) |
265	| 4 | validation failed |
266	| ≥10 | reserved for skill-specific conditions |
267	
268	### Predictable output size
269	
270	Many agent harnesses truncate tool output past ~10-30K characters. If your
271	script can produce large output:
272	
273	- Default to a summary or a sane limit
274	- Provide `--offset` / `--limit` for pagination
275	- Or require `--output FILE` so the agent has to opt in to stdout
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)
280	
281	Stock macOS ships bash 3.2. If the script may run on macOS without Homebrew
282	bash, avoid:
283	
284	| Don't use | Use instead |
285	|---|---|
286	| `mapfile -t arr < file` | `while IFS= read -r line; do arr+=("$line"); done < file` |
287	| `${var,,}` (lowercase) | `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' <<< "$var"` |
288	| `${var^^}` (uppercase) | `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' <<< "$var"` |
289	| `[[ -v VAR ]]` | `[ "${VAR+x}" = "x" ]` |
290	| Associative arrays `declare -A` | indexed array + key parser, or switch to Python |
291	| `wait -n` (wait for any) | `wait` (waits for all) or track PIDs manually |
292	| `&>` redirection | `>file 2>&1` |
293	
294	Lead every script with:
295	
296	```bash
297	#!/usr/bin/env bash
298	set -euo pipefail
299	```
300	
301	`set -u` catches typos in variable names. `set -e` aborts on first error.
302	`set -o pipefail` makes pipelines fail if any stage fails (otherwise only the
303	last stage's exit code matters).
304	
305	If you need bash 4+ features, either:
306	
307	- Switch to Python with PEP 723 (recommended for anything non-trivial).
308	- Add an explicit version check at the top:
309	
310	```bash
311	if (( BASH_VERSINFO[0] < 4 )); then
312	  echo "Error: requires bash >= 4. macOS ships 3.2; install via 'brew install bash'." >&2
313	  exit 1
314	fi
315	```
316	
317	---
318	
319	## Quick script checklist
320	
321	- [ ] Has `#!/usr/bin/env bash` (or equivalent) shebang
322	- [ ] Is `chmod +x`
323	- [ ] Starts with `set -euo pipefail` (bash) or equivalent strict mode
324	- [ ] Responds to `--help` with usage + flags + examples + exit codes
325	- [ ] No interactive prompts; all input via flags / env / stdin
326	- [ ] Errors say *what + expected + try this*
327	- [ ] Data → stdout (structured), diagnostics → stderr
328	- [ ] `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
329	- [ ] Exit codes are distinct and documented
330	- [ ] Pinned versions for any `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
331	- [ ] Python helpers use PEP 723 inline deps (not external `requirements.txt`)
332	- [ ] Bash 3.2 compatible if it might run on stock macOS
333	- [ ] Idempotent where possible
334
```

21	#            ../../.agents/skills/<name> (and any other detected agent dir).

===== script-bash.template =====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SCRIPT_NAME — one-line description.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS] ARGS

One-paragraph description of what this script does.

Options:
  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it.
  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  SCRIPT_NAME foo
  SCRIPT_NAME --dry-run foo

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  invalid arguments
  2  required input missing
EOF
}

# Logging: data → stdout, diagnostics → stderr.
log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

DRY_RUN=0
ARGS=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --) shift; while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do ARGS+=("$1"); shift; done ;;
    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)  ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

if [ "${#ARGS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  die "missing required argument (try --help)" 1
fi

main() {
  local target="${ARGS[0]}"
  log "Processing: $target"

  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] Would do work on: $target"
    return 0
  fi

  # Real work goes here. Emit structured data on stdout.
  printf '{"target":"%s","status":"ok"}\n' "$target"
}

main
===== script-python.template =====
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   # Add deps here, e.g.:
#   # "httpx>=0.27,<1",
# ]
# ///
"""SCRIPT_NAME — one-line description.

Self-contained via PEP 723 inline metadata. Run with `uv run`:

    uv run SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS] ARGS

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  invalid arguments
  2  required input missing
  3  external system failure
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys


def make_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="SCRIPT_NAME",
        description="One-paragraph description of what this script does.",
        epilog=(
            "Examples:\n"
            "  uv run SCRIPT_NAME foo\n"
            "  uv run SCRIPT_NAME --dry-run foo\n"
        ),
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    p.add_argument("target", help="The thing to process.")
    p.add_argument(
        "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Show what would happen without doing it.",
    )
    return p


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    """Diagnostics → stderr."""
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = make_parser().parse_args(argv)

    log(f"Processing: {args.target}")

    if args.dry_run:
        log(f"[dry-run] Would do work on: {args.target}")
        return 0

    # Real work goes here. Emit structured data on stdout.
    json.dump({"target": args.target, "status": "ok"}, sys.stdout)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	---
2	name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap
3	description: Bootstrap MkDocs Material docs sites with optional GitHub Pages deploy, uv-pinned tooling, llms.txt/copy-to-LLM support, page/nav helpers, and mkdocs-static-i18n languages such as zh-TW. Use when the user asks to set up docs, publish docs to GitHub Pages, create an MkDocs site, turn README or markdown notes into a site, add bilingual/multilingual docs, add zh-TW/Traditional Chinese, i18n, or translate docs. Consent-gated; records repo preferences and never auto-migrates existing docs.
4	---
5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
89	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
90	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
91	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
92	
93	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
94	
95	### 4. Scaffold
96	
97	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
98	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
99	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
100	copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
101	`.gitignore` so the generated site is never committed — plus `/.cache/` when
102	`--social` is on.
103	
104	```bash
105	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
106	  --site-name "My Project" \
107	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
108	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
109	```
110	
111	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
112	files unless `--force` is passed.
113	
114	Add `--social` to enable OG/Twitter preview cards (see Gotchas → "Social cards
115	are opt-in"). Leave it off unless the user wants rich link unfurls and can take
116	the Cairo/Pango system dependency; a plain scaffold builds dependency-free.
117	
118	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
119	
120	```bash
121	uv sync --extra docs
122	uv run mkdocs build --strict
123	```
124	
125	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
126	
127	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
128	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
129	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
130	Only proceed on explicit yes.
131	
132	```bash
133	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
134	  --repo owner/repo
135	```
136	
137	Flags:
138	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
139	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
140	
141	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
142	in preferences.
143	
144	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
145	
146	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
147	`mkdocs.yml`:
148	
149	```bash
150	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
151	  --section workflows \
152	  --title "My new workflow" \
153	  --slug my-new-workflow
154	```
155	
156	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
157	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
158	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
159	
160	If the project has additional languages configured in
161	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
162	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
163	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
164	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
165	
166	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
167	
168	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
169	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
170	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
171	
172	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
173	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
174	
175	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
176	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
177	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
178	
179	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
180	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
181	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
182	`Makefile` for you):
183	
184	```bash
185	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
186	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
187	```
188	
189	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
190	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
191	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
192	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
193	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
194	is a no-op.
195	
196	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
197	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
198	
199	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
200	
201	```bash
202	uv sync --extra docs
203	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
204	```
205	
206	#### After the script finishes — translation is a separate step
207	
208	`add-language.sh` only produces **structural placeholders**: each
209	`*.<LANG>.md` stub contains the terminology admonition plus a "Translation
210	pending" warning. The script never auto-translates body prose, because LLM
211	translation routinely violates the "no invented translations" terminology
212	rule (e.g. coining 「嵌入」/「向量」/「内嵌」 for `embedding` when none is
213	canonical).
214	
215	Once stubs exist, **explicitly ask the user whether to translate them now**
216	— do not assume. A reasonable script:
217	
218	> "Stubs created. Want me to translate the bodies page-by-page? I'll do
219	> 4-6 pages per batch, run `mkdocs build` between batches to verify, and
220	> follow the terminology rule (English original on first mention, never
221	> invent translations)."
222	
223	Only proceed on explicit yes. If the user defers, leave the stubs in place
224	— they're already valid pages and the build passes.
225	
226	When translating, also offer to populate `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`
227	for top-level section headings (see `references/i18n-guide.md`
228	§nav_translations). This is independent from page-body translation and the
229	user may want one without the other.

309	
310	## Gotchas
311	
312	- **Social cards (OG previews) are opt-in — off by default.** Pass `--social`
313	  to `init-docs-site.sh` to enable them; a plain scaffold has no social plugin,
314	  no `[imaging]` dep, and no Cairo/Pango CI step, so it builds with zero system
315	  dependencies (a bare `mkdocs build` renders in well under a second). Enable
316	  it when the user wants rich link unfurls and accepts the cost below. To turn
317	  it on for an already-scaffolded site, add the `social` plugin block to
318	  `mkdocs.yml`, `mkdocs-material[imaging]` to the docs deps, the Cairo/Pango +
319	  cache steps to `docs.yml`, and `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` (copy from
320	  `assets/social/*` — the same snippets `--social` injects).
321	- **The `social` plugin needs system Cairo/Pango + the `[imaging]` extra.**
322	  `mkdocs-material[imaging]` pulls cairosvg/pillow, but those bind to system
323	  `libcairo`/`libpango` — without them the build aborts with a libcairo load
324	  error. With `--social`, `docs-workflow.yml.template` apt-installs them
325	  (`libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libfreetype6-dev …`) and caches
326	  `.cache/plugin/social`. Locally: `brew install cairo pango` (macOS) or the
327	  same apt packages (Linux). `--social` also adds `/.cache/` to `.gitignore` —
328	  the plugin writes ~1 card PNG per page (tens of MB) plus a downloaded font
329	  there. Cold build renders one card per page (network-fetches the font from
330	  Google Fonts); warm cache is seconds.
331	- **CJK/arrow page titles render as tofu boxes (□□□) on social cards unless
332	  the card font covers them.** The plugin's default font (Roboto) and plain
333	  "Noto Sans" are Latin-only, so Chinese/Japanese/Korean titles — and even a
334	  `→` in an English title — come out as boxes. `add-language.sh` auto-sets a
335	  CJK-capable `social.cards_layout_options.font_family` (Noto Sans TC/SC/JP/KR)
336	  when you add a CJK language, but only if the social plugin is present and no
337	  font is already set (so scaffold with `--social` *before* adding zh-TW, or
338	  set the font yourself afterward). Verify by opening a rendered
339	  `site/assets/images/social/**/<page>.png`, not just by trusting the build.
340	- **`yq` in these scripts is mikefarah yq (v4), which has NO `if/then/else/end`
341	  syntax** — that's jq. Use `(.plugins[] | select(has("x")) | .x.y) = z` or
342	  `+= […]`, never `.plugins |= map(if has("x") then … else . end)` (it dies
343	  with a `lexer: invalid input text "if …"` error). This bit the i18n
344	  second-language append path historically; keep new expressions in the
345	  `select()` form.
346	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
347	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
348	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
349	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
350	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
351	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
352	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
353	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
354	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
355	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
356	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
357	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
358	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
359	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
360	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
361	  Counter-intuitive name.
362	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
363	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
364	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
365	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
366	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
367	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
368	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
369	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
370	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
371	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
372	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
373	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
374	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
375	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
376	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
377	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
378	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
379	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
380	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
381	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
382	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
383	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
384	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
385	  is just acting on it.
386	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
387	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
388	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
389	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
390	
391	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
392	
393	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
394	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
395	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
396	have customizations the templates don't know about.
397

```text
1	---
2	name: verifiable-surfaces
3	description: 'Design and verify exercisable surfaces on apps, CLIs, services, and config. Use when authoring a new CLI/tool/library/service in Python (uv + tyro / click / argparse), Node (commander/yargs), or Bash to ensure it exposes `--help`, `--dry-run`, `--print-config`, isolated-state smoke entrypoints, and explicit exit-code contracts. Also use when editing app/tool config, CLI args/env parsing, dotfiles such as chezmoi, Ansible playbooks, CI/deploy manifests, or generated/rendered config — forces syntax/schema, then app-native loader/parser/debug/dry-run, then narrowest harmless runtime smoke. The invariant: a surface that cannot be exercised cheaply and harmlessly was not actually verified, regardless of how much linting passed.'
4	---
5	
6	# Verifiable Surfaces
7	
8	Apply this skill in two complementary modes:
9	
10	- **Authoring mode** — when creating or extending a CLI, tool, library, or
11	  service, design surfaces that can be exercised cheaply and harmlessly:
12	  `--help`, `--dry-run`, `--print-config`, isolated-state smoke, explicit
13	  exit codes.
14	- **Verification mode** — when editing config, CLI arg/env parsing, dotfiles,
15	  Ansible, IaC, or any rendered/generated config, walk the verification
16	  ladder until the highest *harmless* gate has passed.
17	
18	## Core Invariant
19	
20	A surface that cannot be exercised cheaply and harmlessly was not actually
21	verified. Syntax checks, type checks, and lints are necessary but not
22	sufficient. If the program has its own loader, dry-run, or check command, run
23	it. If it does not have one, your authoring job is to add one.
24	
25	## When To Use
26	
27	**Authoring mode:**
28	
29	- Writing a new Python CLI with uv + tyro, click, typer, or argparse
30	- Writing a new Node CLI with commander, yargs, or oclif
31	- Writing a new Bash script that takes args or has side effects
32	- Adding a new subcommand, flag, or env var to an existing tool
33	- Building a service/daemon with a config file
34	- Building an SDK/library that loads config or accepts complex inputs
35	
36	**Verification mode:**
37	
38	- Editing app/tool config: `next.config.*`, `components.json`, `.prettierrc`,
39	  `pyproject.toml`, `ruff.toml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `mkdocs.yml`,
40	  `pueue.yml`, DVC/MLflow config, service manifests
41	- Changing CLI argument parsing, env var parsing, config discovery order, or
42	  defaults that are only exercised after startup
43	- Updating dotfiles or generated config, especially chezmoi templates,
44	  shell init files, editor config, Git hooks, launchd/systemd units, or
45	  files that depend on `$HOME`, platform, hostname, or secrets
46	- Editing Ansible, Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker Compose, CI, deploy, or
47	  other automation where parse success can still fail at plan/apply/runtime
48	- Debugging "works in lint/build, breaks when the tool starts" failures
49	
50	## When NOT To Use
51	
52	- Pure documentation edits with no executable or loaded configuration
53	- Formatting-only edits where the tool's own formatter is the requested end
54	  state and no behavior changes
55	- Production deploy validation that needs credentials or live infra access the
56	  user has not approved. Stop at a harmless local smoke and report the gap.
57	
58	## Authoring Mode: Design Verifiable Surfaces
59	
60	Every CLI/tool/service surface you add must satisfy this checklist:
61	
62	1. **`--help` is mandatory.** Show usage, every flag, examples, and exit
63	   codes. The agent (and the next human) reads this first.
64	2. **`--dry-run` for any side effect.** File writes, network calls, database
65	   mutations, config edits, deploys, restarts. Dry-run must still load the
66	   real config and resolve the real plan, not short-circuit before parsing.
67	3. **`--print-config` / `--show-config` for config-loading programs.** Print
68	   the fully resolved config (after env/file/CLI merging) so the user can
69	   diff what the program actually sees vs. what they edited.
70	4. **Isolated-state smoke entrypoint.** The tool must accept `--config <path>`
71	   and respect `$HOME` / `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` overrides; never hard-code
72	   `~/.foo`. This lets `env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) ...` exercise the real load
73	   path with zero blast radius.
74	5. **Explicit exit-code contract.** `0` for success; non-zero for failure
75	   classes (`1` runtime/user error, `2` usage error is a common convention).
76	   Document the codes in `--help`.
77	6. **Structured stdout, diagnostics on stderr.** Stdout is the program's
78	   data output (parseable when reasonable). Logs, progress, and errors go
79	   to stderr so callers can pipe stdout safely.
80	7. **Self-verification after authoring.** Before declaring done, run:
81	   `cmd --help`, `cmd --dry-run <smallest input>`, `cmd --print-config`
82	   (if applicable), an intentionally-bad input to confirm non-zero exit,
83	   and one isolated-state smoke (`env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) ...`).
84	
85	See `references/authoring-checklist.md` for concrete templates per
86	language (Python tyro/click, Node commander/yargs, Bash).
87	
88	## Verification Mode: Verification Ladder
89	
90	Pick the highest safe rung that exercises the actual failure mode. Do not
91	stop at a lower rung when the next harmless rung exists.
92	
93	1. **Syntax/schema gate** — `yamllint`, `jsonschema`, `ansible-playbook
94	   --syntax-check`, `terraform validate`, `docker compose config`,
95	   `mkdocs build`, `tsc --noEmit`.
96	2. **Rendered/applied config gate** — render templates and generated files,
97	   then validate those outputs. For chezmoi, inspect `chezmoi diff`,
98	   `chezmoi apply --dry-run --verbose`, or `chezmoi execute-template`; do
99	   not validate only the `.tmpl` source.
100	3. **App/tool-native loader gate** — prefer the command the app itself
101	   exposes: `config check`, `doctor`, `debug`, `--print-config`,
102	   `--show-config`, `--dry-run`, `--check`, `validate`, `plan`, or a small
103	   script that imports and loads the same config module used at startup.
104	4. **Compile/build gate** — when config influences generated code, bundling,
105	   routing, plugins, import paths, or type definitions, run the narrowest
106	   compile/build that loads it.
107	5. **Harmless runtime smoke** — for runtime-only failures, run the narrowest
108	   local smoke with isolated state: `/tmp`, temp `$HOME`, temp config path,
109	   temp database/file store, local container, `--check`, `--dry-run`,
110	   limited tag, limited target, or loopback-only service.
111	
112	Record which rung you reached. If you cannot reach the app-native loader or
113	runtime smoke safely, say so explicitly and explain what is still untested.
114	
115	See `references/config-examples.md` for concrete commands per ecosystem
116	(Ansible, chezmoi, JS/TS, Python settings, Docker Compose, Kubernetes,
117	Terraform/OpenTofu, generic loaders).
118	
119	## Default Workflow
120	
121	1. Identify which mode applies. Authoring (new surface) and verification
122	   (changed surface) often co-occur — handle both.
123	2. **Authoring**: walk the 7-point checklist above. Stub out missing items
124	   before the change is "done."
125	3. **Verification**: list the minimum ladder for this change, then run the
126	   lowest cheap gate first and continue until the highest harmless gate has
127	   passed.
128	4. When a gate fails, fix the cause and re-run all earlier affected gates.
129	5. Summarize the exact commands and the highest gate passed.
130	
131	## Ansible Rule
132	
133	`ansible-playbook --syntax-check` is only the first step. It does not execute
134	tasks, evaluate all runtime conditions, contact targets, validate module side
135	effects, or prove variables are correct for the selected hosts. If a
136	playbook, role, inventory, or variable change can fail at execution time, run
137	the narrowest relevant smoke: `--check`, `--diff`, `--tags`, `--skip-tags`,
138	`--limit`, localhost/container inventory, or a role-specific test harness.
139	
140	## Gotchas
141	
142	- **A surface without `--dry-run` is a surface you cannot rehearse.** When
143	  authoring, add it before the destructive code path, not after.
144	- **`--help` must list exit codes and side effects.** "What does this
145	  command do?" should be answerable without reading source.
146	- **Validate rendered config, not just source templates.** Template syntax
147	  can pass while the rendered file has invalid paths, missing env vars,
148	  duplicate keys, or host-specific values the app rejects.
149	- **The app's own loader is the authority.** Generic YAML/JSON/TOML parsing
150	  does not catch semantic errors such as unsupported keys, wrong plugin
151	  names, invalid enum values, env interpolation bugs, or changed default
152	  paths.
153	- **Dry-run must still load.** A no-op preview that never invokes the real
154	  parser is not enough. Prefer dry-runs that render, resolve includes, load
155	  plugins, and build the final plan/config.
156	- **Runtime-only failures need harmless smoke.** Use temp dirs, temp `$HOME`,
157	  temp config files, local containers, check mode, or tag/target narrowing
158	  rather than skipping runtime validation entirely.
159	- **Secrets and machine-specific config require isolation.** Do not read or
160	  write real home-directory state, cloud resources, production inventories,
161	  or credentialed endpoints unless the user explicitly asked for that
162	  level.
163	- **Report the gap, not false confidence.** If only syntax validation was
164	  safe, say "syntax passed; loader/runtime not exercised" and name the
165	  command that should be run in the right environment.
